proj-1.title: Dip – Give LLMs Eyes
proj-1.description: 1st Place, Google DeepMind Gemini Track – Cursor AI Hackathon Hamburg (Feb 2026, 400+ participants). A tool that gives LLMs real-time visual context of the user's screen, eliminating the need to manually describe on-screen content.
proj-1.longDescription:
Dip was created at the Cursor AI Hackathon Hamburg in February 2026 with over 400 participants. The tool gives LLMs real-time visual context by capturing the user's screen and providing it as context to the model. This completely eliminates the need to manually describe on-screen content.

The architecture is based on a Python backend that processes screen captures via the Google Gemini API. A lightweight client captures screen content and sends it to the LLM context.
highlights: 400+ participants at Cursor AI Hackathon Hamburg
Real-time screen capture as LLM context
Eliminates manual description of screen content
proj-1.learnings: Learned how to efficiently feed multimodal AI models with real-time image data while minimizing latency. Experience with screen capture APIs and the Gemini Vision API.

proj-2.title: Mindflayer – Semantic Social Media Filter
proj-2.description: 1st Place Overall ($2,000 prize) – CodeRabbit × Windsurf Hackathon (Dec 2025, 110 participants). A Chrome extension using Gemini to semantically filter social media posts in real-time.
proj-2.longDescription:
Mindflayer is a Chrome extension that semantically filters social media posts in real-time. Instead of keyword-based filtering, it analyzes the actual content and context of posts — powered by Google Gemini.

The project won 1st Place Overall at the CodeRabbit × Windsurf Hackathon with a $2,000 prize. The extension analyzes posts directly in the browser and hides unwanted content without requiring complex filter rules.
highlights: Real-time semantic filtering instead of keyword-based
Seamless browser integration as Chrome extension
proj-2.learnings: Built deep understanding of Chrome Extension API and content scripts. Learned how to efficiently use AI models in browser contexts and minimize latency in real-time filtering.

proj-3.title: Airbn – AI Property Management
proj-3.description: 1st Place Arbio Track, 3rd Overall – {Tech: Europe} Hackathon Berlin (Jan 2026). An AI-native property management platform with microservices architecture, voice-first guest support, and automated damage detection via OpenCV.
proj-3.longDescription:
Airbn is an AI-native property management platform created at the {Tech: Europe} Hackathon in Berlin. The platform combines multiple microservices: voice-first guest support via WhatsApp, automatic damage detection via OpenCV, and intelligent property management features.

The architecture uses GPT-4o for natural conversations, OpenCV for image analysis of damage reports, and a combination of Flask, FastAPI, and Node.js for the various backend services.
proj-3.learnings: Gained experience with microservices architecture under time pressure. Learned how to use WhatsApp Business API for voice-first interactions and OpenCV for practical damage detection.

proj-4.title: Hundewelt.space – AI Dog Blog
proj-4.description: Fully automated German dog blog with AI content pipeline. Next.js frontend with SSR, search, RSS, and admin dashboard. Python LangGraph pipeline for topic research, article generation, image generation, and automatic publishing.
proj-4.longDescription:
Hundewelt.space is a fully automated German dog blog with a complete AI content pipeline. The Next.js frontend offers SSR, full-text search, RSS feeds, and an admin dashboard.

The core is a Python LangGraph pipeline that automatically researches topics, generates articles, creates matching images, and publishes everything automatically. A newsletter system with double opt-in rounds out the project.
highlights: Next.js SSR frontend with search and RSS
proj-4.learnings: Extensive experience with LangGraph for complex, multi-step AI workflows. Learned how to build a fully automated content pipeline from topic research to publication.

proj-5.title: Video Journal Analyzer
proj-5.description: A web app for analyzing video URLs with two modes: diary entry analysis (emotions and moods) and rhetoric coach (speaking style, articulation, improvement suggestions).
proj-5.longDescription:
The Video Journal Analyzer is a web app that analyzes video URLs in two modes:

1. Diary Entry Analysis: Detects emotions and moods from video diaries and provides structured feedback.

2. Rhetoric Coach: Analyzes speaking style, articulation, and body language with concrete improvement suggestions.

The frontend is built with Next.js and TypeScript using Tailwind CSS for styling.
highlights: Two analysis modes: emotion analysis and rhetoric coaching
Structured feedback with concrete improvement suggestions
proj-5.learnings: Experience with video analysis APIs and processing multimodal content. Learned how to present complex analysis results in a user-friendly way.

proj-6.title: Song Splitter
proj-6.description: An audio tool for splitting songs into individual components such as drums, guitar, bass, vocals, and other instruments using AI-powered audio source separation.
proj-6.longDescription:
Song Splitter is an audio tool that splits songs into individual components — drums, guitar, bass, vocals, and other instruments. The tool uses AI-powered audio source separation with Spleeter and Demucs.

The workflow is simple: upload a song, start separation, download individual tracks. FFmpeg is used for audio processing and conversion.
highlights: Support for Spleeter and Demucs models
Separation into drums, guitar, bass, vocals and more
proj-6.learnings: Built deep understanding of audio processing and AI-based source separation. Experience with FFmpeg for audio manipulation and the differences between Spleeter and Demucs.
